page: Amazon Web Services c6g.xlarge is a compute-optimized ARM64 instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance features 4 physical cores and 4 vCPUs powered by an AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.5 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core mapping. Hardware specifications include 8.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU), a 32 MB L3 cache, hardware AES encryption support, and 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not include local NVMe storage or discrete GPU accelerators.

Performance evaluation highlights moderate single-core execution paired with lower multi-core and memory subsystem throughput relative to x86 alternatives. Synthetic benchmarks register a single-core stress-ng result of 1519.79 and a Geekbench single-core score of 965.0. Uncached memory performance achieves 71.99 GB/sec read and 35.14 GB/sec write bandwidth. Heavy multi-threaded operations yield a Geekbench multi-core score of 3252.0 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 6053.66. Application-level benchmarks show 4.76 million Redis SET operations per second, a static web serving throughput of 4.95 GB/sec, and 135M parameter LLM inference rates of 145.31 prompt tokens per second.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides hardware density tailored for ARM-native software execution without x86 vector extensions like AVX-512. While lower per-core memory and moderate multi-threaded benchmark figures limit its use for heavy compute clusters or large in-memory databases, the hardware profile offers cost-efficient scaling for containerized microservices, web applications, caching tiers, and build servers.
description: Amazon Web Services c6g.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance utilizing 4 dedicated ARM64 Neoverse-N1 physical cores operating at 2.5 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Configured with 8.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core), 32 MB of L3 cache, and 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, this instance omits local ephemeral storage and GPU acceleration. Benchmark evaluations show single-threaded performance with uncached memory bandwidth reaching 71.99 GB/sec read and 35.14 GB/sec write speeds. However, multi-core scores remain moderate, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 3252.0 and PassMark CPU score of 2702.45. Application tests demonstrate static web serving throughput of 4.95 GB/sec and Redis SET performance of 4.76 million operations per second. The instance offers a balanced profile for ARM-native microservices, lightweight web servers, caching layers, and CI/CD build environments.
